  \caption{\textbf{Taxonomic and anatomical constraint enforcement and ancestor relaxation across six eukaryotes.} The stress cohort of each species contains every protein that carries at least one real blind predictor claim from the multikingdom benchmark (DIAMOND transfer from a reference set without same-species or same-genus hits, and Pfam-to-GO mapping). One cross-clade developmental claim (raw score $0.82$--$0.95$) is injected into $300$ randomly chosen cohort proteins per species ($44$ for \textit{P.~patens}), and $20\%$ of the true, species-appropriate developmental claims scoring above $0.62$ are attenuated into $[0.55, 0.62]$. Violation columns give the protein--term predictions with posterior $\ge 0.50$ whose term is forbidden for the species under unconstrained Stage 0 pooling, direct GO taxon rules, the Stage 1 soft anatomical prior, and Stage 2A enforcement by deletion and by ancestor relaxation (percentage of Stage 0 violations eliminated in parentheses). Pooled micro $F_{\max}$ is evaluated against the unmodified Swiss-Prot annotations on all cohort proteins (propagated recall in parentheses) and on the injected proteins, under Stage 0 pooling, Stage 2A deletion, and Stage 2A relaxation. IC retained is the mean information content of the terms above $0.50$ after relaxation relative to Stage 0 on the injected proteins. Developmental rescue counts attenuated claims recovered above $0.50$ under relaxation. The last row runs the unperturbed real claims through the same configurations and reports endogenous violations and CAFA protein-centric $F_{\max}$ (Stage 0 / deletion / relaxation) over the Swiss-Prot panel of each species ($1{,}200$ proteins; $155$ for \textit{P.~patens}).}
